Host and player: organized, welcoming, first-time facilitator; wants to play fairly while tracking everyone. Notices divided attention and practical timing.
Enthusiastic amateur sleuth: likes comparing evidence, takes concise notes, does not assume the loudest suspect is guilty.
Sociable guest: came for friends and costumes, listens but is easily distracted by conversations; gives material a normal casual reading.
Quiet first-timer: willing to read prepared answers, anxious about improvising and asking someone the wrong question.
Competitive puzzle fan: methodical, tests contradictions, wants a satisfying deduction rather than an obvious answer.
Theatrical extrovert: enjoys performing the character and riffing, but must not invent factual evidence. Tests the boundary between acting and answers.
Older guest with reading fatigue: comfortable reading clearly printed large text, dislikes long dense instructions; evaluates note-taking and page navigation.
Literal rule follower: careful about IF branches and round boundaries; flags ambiguous verbs and conflicting instructions.
Distracted dinner guest: sociable and well intentioned, limited working memory for names and times; uses provided note space without perfect recall.
Suspicious contrarian: challenges the reliability of records, considers alternative explanations but accepts explicit fictional constraints.
Museum lover: invested in theme, character relationships and clues as objects; notices when the deduction feels like bookkeeping.
Practical skeptic: wants simple rules, dislikes paperwork and waiting; assesses whether rounds feel repetitive.
Empathetic roleplayer: tries to understand motives, shares observations with others; can be drawn toward emotional suspects.
Confident novice: skims instructions first, follows host prompts; notices things a quick reader could accidentally disclose.
Careful note taker: creates a small comparison of testimony, checks all three strands before voting.
Optional-role newcomer: has fewer core relationships, wants equal participation and enough context without inside knowledge.
